behaviors.description: One thing a command asks, and how many queries it names. Unless exactly one, the problem is one-query.
behaviors.name: Asks

otherwise.does: How a command branches into cases. If Layer 1 wrote the cases: an outcome written outside the cases (`flat`) is the problem flat-in-cases, and a goTo, does or responds Layer 1 wrote outside the cases (`layer1Outcome`) is the problem layer1-outside-cases (both may be reported, in that order). Otherwise, if the interpretation wrote the cases: `flat` is the problem flat-in-cases, and a goTo Layer 1 wrote (`layer1GoTo`) is the problem branch-over-goto (both may be reported, in that order). If nobody wrote cases, there is no problem.

emits.onlyWhen: Someone (Layer 1 or the interpretation) wrote the cases, and an outcome is written outside the cases (`flat`)
Layer 1 wrote the cases, and Layer 1 wrote a goTo, does or responds outside the cases
Layer 1 did not write the cases, the interpretation did, and Layer 1 wrote a goTo

behaviors.description: A command calls a contained component. If there is no such component, the problem is no-part. Otherwise, if it is one of many (`keyedPart`) but no key was written, the problem is key-missing; if it is a single component but a key was written, the problem is key-extra.
behaviors.name: Call

behaviors.description: An entry the interpretation wrote into a group (a datum, a command, a case, ...). If Layer 1 lists that group's entries (`listed`), the group is closed to new entries (`closed`), and Layer 1 does not have this one, the problem is closed.
behaviors.name: Entry

behaviors.description: A key the interpretation wrote. If it cannot be written there (`known` is false), the problem is unknown-key.
behaviors.name: Key

behaviors.description: One place, and whether Layer 1 and the interpretation each wrote it. If it is not a place that can be written (`known` is false), the problem is unknown-key; otherwise, if both wrote it, the problem is conflict (Layer 1 wins, and the interpretation may not write over it).
behaviors.name: Slot

behaviors.description: The hash of Layer 1 recorded in the interpretation (if any) and the hash of Layer 1 now. If one was recorded and it differs, the problem is stale.
behaviors.name: Stamp

behaviors.description: A state Layer 1 listed by name. If it has no description, the problem is undescribed.
behaviors.name: State

descriptions.component: Reports the problems found when an interpretation is laid over Layer 1, one fact at a time.
descriptions.effects.Problem: A problem shown by the fact just given.
